description: A --state seed, --resume last --force: a resume: restart dynamic `d` drops its stale `x`/`reader`/`sibling_bare_reader` and reruns, so a bare {{d.x.value}} inside `d` reads the fresh node, same as {{prime.d.x.value}} -- this pair already resolved on main, an ordinary ancestor-context read, never the fallback, since `d` was already a live top-level key there. A second reader in the same restarted `d`, {{x.value}} (no `d.` prefix), needs the actual bare-sibling-reference fallback to reach that same fresh `x` instead of nothing; a plain dynamic `e`'s unfinished `first` reruns and reads its already-completed, saved sibling `second` bare, same as dotted, needing the same fallback. Both of those two reads -- `d`'s own `{{x.value}}` and `e`'s own `{{second.value}}` -- render empty on main, which never resolved a bare sibling reference inside any dynamic at all; only the pre-existing `{{d.x.value}}`/`{{prime.d.x.value}}` pair already worked there. Python-only: the conformance harness always invokes electricity through its legacy positional form, which has no `--state` of its own (#752's precedent); `test_run_cli_parity.py` covers this restart-and-saved-state shape, bare and dotted, on both engines' own `run` subcommand instead.
